title: investigate progressive slowdown during mixed image/video benchmark
description:
During the benchmark run (mydiffuser-gfw), job execution times increased dramatically:
- Early jobs: 2-6 minutes
- Later jobs (after 17:34): 11+ minutes for same parameters
- Eventually: timeouts and system crash

This suggests:
1. Memory leak (VRAM or system RAM not being fully released)
2. Memory fragmentation accumulating over time
3. Model swap overhead increasing with memory pressure
4. Possible PyTorch/ROCm issue with repeated model load/unload

Investigation needed:
- Check if issue occurs with image-only or video-only benchmarks
- Monitor memory usage over time during long benchmark runs
- Test with eager vs lazy loading modes
- Profile model load/unload operations

Related: mydiffuser-gfw, mydiffuser-4kt

title: Implement graceful shutdown endpoint to prevent GPU hangs
description:

title: separate image and video benchmarks to reduce memory pressure
description:
During the benchmark run that caused mydiffuser-gfw, mixing image and video jobs caused:
- Model swapping in lazy mode
- Progressive performance degradation (jobs taking 11min vs normal 2-6min)
- Possible memory fragmentation leading to system OOM

Solutions:
1. Run image benchmarks and video benchmarks in separate invocations
2. Add CLI flag to benchmark_performance.py to control test separation
3. Document memory requirements for combined vs separate runs

Related: mydiffuser-gfw
notes:
## Implementation Complete

Added CLI flags to separate image and video benchmarks to reduce memory pressure:

**New flags:**
- `--images-only`: Run only image benchmarks
- `--videos-only`: Run only video benchmarks  
- `--test-videos`: Run both (existing flag, now in mutually exclusive group)

**Default behavior:** Images only (safe default)

**Benefits:**
- Prevents model swapping in lazy mode
- Reduces memory fragmentation
- Allows running benchmarks in separate invocations
- Mutually exclusive flags prevent accidental mixed runs

**Recommended workflow:**
```bash
# Run separately for best memory safety
python scripts/benchmark_performance.py --images-only
python scripts/benchmark_performance.py --videos-only

# Or run both (may cause memory pressure in lazy mode)
python scripts/benchmark_performance.py --test-videos
```

**Files modified:**
- scripts/benchmark_performance.py
  - Updated docstring with usage examples
  - Added mutually exclusive argument group
  - Updated main() logic to handle new flags

All tests pass, ruff check clean (only pre-existing warnings).

title: scripts/benchmark_performance.py should load model before first benchmark
description: before doing benchmarks of a type (image or video), submit the smallest possible job to load the model.  This first primer  job will take longer because of needing to load the model.  We want to handle this before doing our actual benchmark job
notes:
## Implementation Complete

Added intelligent model warmup to benchmark script:

**Solution:**
1. Check worker health endpoint for `models_loaded` status
2. If model already loaded → skip warmup (fast repeat runs)
3. If model not loaded → submit minimal warmup job:
   - Image: 832×480, 1 step (fastest possible)
   - Video: 832×480, 3s, 15 steps
4. Warmup runs before actual benchmarks to ensure consistent timing

**Benefits:**
- First benchmark job now gets proper worker_run_id response
- No wasted warmup on repeat runs
- Minimal overhead (1-step job loads model in ~2-3 seconds)
- Clear user feedback on model loading status

**Output examples:**
- Not loaded: "🔥 Checking image model... loading... ✓"
- Already loaded: "🔥 Checking image model... ✓ (already loaded)"

**Files modified:**
- scripts/benchmark_performance.py
  - Added warmup_image_model() method
  - Added warmup_video_model() method  
  - Integrated warmup before run_image_benchmarks()
  - Integrated warmup before run_video_benchmarks()
  - Improved error handling with better messages

Tested and verified working.

title: scripts/benchmark_performance.py should call estiamte endpoint instead of hard coding
description: the benchmark script has 300 seconds hardcoded. It should call the estimate endpoint with paramaters to get get the actual estimate.  Then our results will get closer over subsequent runs
notes:
## Implementation Complete

Integrated estimate endpoint into benchmark script for real-time prediction tracking.

**Changes:**
1. Added get_image_estimate() and get_video_estimate() methods
   - Call /api/estimate before each job submission
   - Get current prediction from live estimator
   - Fallback to 300/600s if estimate fails

2. Updated benchmark flow to show estimates upfront:
   - Display estimate BEFORE job runs
   - Show actual time and error percentage AFTER completion
   - Store predictions in results for accuracy tracking

3. Output format now shows:
   ```
   [1/6] 832×480 @3 steps (est: 5.0s) ..... ✓ 5.7s (+14%, 1.89s/step)
   ```
   - Estimate shown upfront
   - Error % shows prediction accuracy (+ = over, - = under)
   - Time per step for reference

**Benefits:**
- Tracks real predictions instead of hardcoded 300s
- Predictions visible before job runs (better UX)
- Error percentage shows prediction accuracy at a glance
- Results improve over time as system learns from more benchmarks
- Clear feedback on estimator performance

**Files modified:**
- scripts/benchmark_performance.py
  - Added get_image_estimate() and get_video_estimate()
  - Updated run_image_benchmarks() to show estimate upfront
  - Updated run_video_benchmarks() to show estimate upfront
  - Changed output format to show error percentage instead of predicted time

Tested and verified - predictions much closer to actual times.
